note: RESOURCES-R2: the state process for /getting-a-medical-card/<state>/ as at most 8 plain claims per state, each from the official program page in url, fetched on 'retrieved'. 'quote' is the page wording as returned by the fetch (FACTS-R2 re-checks every claim against its url). No advice: what the program says, nothing more.

mississippi.claim: A patient qualifies with one of the conditions listed by the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program (for example cancer, Parkinson's disease, PTSD or diabetic/peripheral neuropathy), or a chronic, terminal or debilitating condition or its treatment that produces effects such as chronic pain, seizures or severe nausea.
mississippi.quote: The following medical conditions or their treatment qualify for participation in the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program: cancer, Parkinson's disease, ... post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), ... diabetic/peripheral neuropathy ... Also qualifying is a chronic terminal or debilitating disease or medical condition or its treatment that produces one or more of the following: cachexia or wasting syndrome, chronic pain, severe or intractable nausea, seizures, ...

mississippi.claim: The condition must be certified by a licensed MD, DO, nurse practitioner, physician assistant or optometrist registered with the Mississippi State Department of Health; practitioners do not write a prescription, and the Department issues the card.
mississippi.quote: they must be a licensed practitioner (MD, DO, Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, or Optometrist) that has been registered with the Mississippi State Department of Health ... Practitioners do not actually write a prescription for medical cannabis. The MS State Department of Health actually issues the medical cannabis identification cards to patients.

mississippi.claim: An initial certification can only be obtained after an in-person visit.
mississippi.quote: You can only obtain an initial certification following an initial in-person visit.

mississippi.claim: There is no application fee; the card carries a non-refundable fee of $25.00, or $15.00 for Medicaid participants, and disabled veterans and disabled first responders with proper documentation can get a fee waiver. Seeing the practitioner has its own cost.
mississippi.quote: There is no application fee, but there is a standard non-refundable fee of $25.00 and a non-refundable fee of $15.00 for Medicaid Participants. Disabled Veterans and Disabled First Responders with proper documentation are eligible for a fee waiver. Please note that there is a cost associated with seeing a registered practitioner to certify the condition.

mississippi.claim: Applications are reviewed for completeness and correctness within 10 days, status can be checked in the MMCP Licensing Portal, and approved patients' cards are made available within five days.
mississippi.quote: Your application will be reviewed for completeness and correctness within 10 days of submission. You can check your application status online through the MMCP Licensing Portal. ... Upon approval of a patient application, patient identification cards are made available within five (5) days.

mississippi.claim: The certification is good for one year unless the practitioner limits the timeframe.
mississippi.quote: The certification is good for one (1) year unless the practitioner limits the timeframe.

mississippi.claim: For a patient under 18, the certification may only be issued by a physician (MD/DO), and the caregiver must be the child's primary custodial parent or legal guardian.
mississippi.quote: A certification issued for a minor (under the age of 18) may only be issued by a physician (MD/DO). Caregivers for minor patients MUST be the child’s primary custodial parent or legal guardian.

mississippi.claim: People living in another state can apply if they medically qualify and hold an active medical cannabis identification card in their home state; those cards are valid for fifteen days.
mississippi.quote: Yes. They must medically qualify and have an active identification card for the use of medical cannabis in his/her state of residence. Applications can be made up to thirty (30) days before arriving in Mississippi, and cards are valid for fifteen (15) days.

oklahoma.claim: The Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority (OMMA) licenses patients: residents aged 18 and up are eligible for an adult patient license, and residents aged 17 and younger for a minor patient license.
oklahoma.quote: Oklahoma residents age 18 and up are eligible for a medical marijuana adult patient license ... Oklahoma residents age 17 and younger are eligible for a medical marijuana minor patient license

oklahoma.claim: An adult applicant provides proof of identity, proof of residency, an acceptable photo and a Physician Recommendation Form (Adult Patient) signed by an authorized physician.
oklahoma.quote: with proof of identity, proof of residency, an acceptable photo ... a signed Physician Recommendation Form (Adult Patient) from an authorized physician.

oklahoma.claim: A minor patient's Physician Recommendation Form must be signed by two registered physicians.
oklahoma.quote: a Physician Recommendation Form (Minor Patient) signed by two registered physicians.

oklahoma.claim: The non-refundable patient license application fee is $100 plus a $4.30 card processing fee, or $20 plus $2.50 with proof of enrollment in Medicaid or Medicare, or status as a 100% disabled veteran.
oklahoma.quote: The nonrefundable patient license application fee is $100 plus a $4.30 credit card processing fee or $20 plus a $2.50 credit card processing fee for people with proof of enrollment in Medicaid or Medicare, or status as a 100% disabled veteran.

oklahoma.claim: OMMA processes patient license applications within 14 business days, as state law requires.
oklahoma.quote: State law requires OMMA to process patient license applications within 14 business days

oklahoma.claim: Adult patient licenses are valid for two years; short-term in-state licenses are valid for 60 days.
oklahoma.quote: Licenses are valid for two years. ... Short-term, in-state licenses are valid for 60 days.

oklahoma.claim: There is no application fee for a caregiver license.
oklahoma.quote: There is no application fee for a caregiver license application.

maryland.claim: Patients register with the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) first, through its OneStop portal, before seeing a provider.
maryland.quote: Visit the MCA registry (OneStop Portal) and click Register and create an account ... you are ready to visit a provider registered with MCA to obtain a valid written certification.

maryland.claim: Individuals 18 years or older may register to take part in the medical cannabis program.
maryland.quote: individuals 18 years or older may register to participate in the program.

maryland.claim: Registration needs proof that the applicant lives in Maryland, a valid government-issued photo ID, a recent photo and a full Social Security number, with all documents dated within the past 90 days.
maryland.quote: Proof that applicant lives in Maryland ... Full 9- digit Social Security Number ... An electronic copy of a valid government-issued photo ID ... A recent clear photo on a white or off white background ... All documents must be dated within the past 90 days.

maryland.claim: After registering, the patient obtains a written certification from a provider registered with the MCA, who issues it using the patient's MCA Patient ID Number.
maryland.quote: patients must obtain a valid written certification from a provider registered with the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

maryland.claim: A plastic patient ID card costs $25 after approval, a paper copy can be printed at no charge, and the $25 fee can be waived for patients enrolled in Maryland Medical Assistance or the VA Maryland Health Care System.
maryland.quote: Maryland Cannabis Administration medical patient ID cards can be ordered after the application is approved for a fee of $25. ... Patients have the option to print a paper copy of their medical cannabis ID cards at no charge. ... you are eligible for a waiver of the $25 fee for the patient ID card

maryland.claim: A written certification that is not used to buy medical cannabis within 120 days of issuance becomes null and void.
maryland.quote: within 120 days of issuance becomes null and void.

maryland.claim: At a licensed dispensary, patients show a government-issued photo ID with their patient ID card or number, and each purchase is limited to a thirty-day supply.
maryland.quote: Visit a licensed Maryland dispensary. ... a government-issued photo ID along with their patient ID card or ID number ... a thirty-day supply

maryland.claim: Minor patients must have at least one caregiver at all times; only parents or legal guardians aged 21 or older can be a minor's caregiver, and the caregiver registers first.
maryland.quote: Minor patients are required to have at least one caregiver assigned to their accounts at all times. Only parents or legal guardians 21 years of age and older are eligible to serve as caregivers for minor patients. Caregivers must register with the MCA prior to registering the minor patient.

new-york.claim: After an in-person or telehealth consultation, a New York State certifying health care provider can certify a patient for any condition the provider deems suitable.
new-york.quote: After consulting with a New York State certifying health care provider via in-person or telehealth ... for any condition deemed suitable by the provider.

new-york.claim: The certification includes a registry ID that can be used immediately, together with a government-issued photo ID, to buy medical cannabis.
new-york.quote: can be used immediately in conjunction with a government issued photo ID

new-york.claim: There is no fee to become a patient in the program.
new-york.quote: There is no fee to become a patient in the program.

new-york.claim: At the dispensary, bring your signed patient certification (on paper or on a phone or device) and a government-issued ID.
new-york.quote: Your signed patient certification (paper copy or displayed on a smart phone or device) ... A government-issued ID

new-york.claim: A patient may designate up to five caregivers to help buy or administer their medical cannabis.
new-york.quote: designate up to five (5) caregivers to assist in purchasing and/or administering

new-york.claim: Medical cannabis products may not be transported outside New York State.
new-york.quote: Medical cannabis products and plants for home cultivation may not be transported outside of New York State.
